Best iPhone and iPad calendar apps for iCloud, Google, Outlook and weather

Four apps stand out: Fantastical, Calendars by Readdle, Calendar 366, and Apple's built-in Apple Calendar.

The important distinction is whether the app displays weather inside your calendar or merely lets you check weather in a separate app or through a workaround.

*Apple Calendar officially supports iCloud, Google and Microsoft Exchange. Outlook.com compatibility may depend on how the Microsoft account is configured. Weather availability and premium entitlements vary by app.

These distinctions are supported by the developers' current documentation and Apple's account-setup guidance. 
App Store
+4

Detailed recommendations
1. Fantastical

Best for advanced scheduling and weather-aware planning

Combines iCloud, Google, Exchange and Microsoft 365 calendars. AccuWeather forecasts appear within the calendar, with event-location weather details, RealFeel and minute-by-minute precipitation features in Premium.

Free: 3-day forecast. Premium: 10-day forecast and advanced weather details. 
Flexibits
+1

Trade-off: Its most useful scheduling and weather features require a subscription.

Official feature and pricing comparison

2. Calendars by Readdle

Best for straightforward all-in-one planning

Readdle explicitly supports Google, Outlook and iCloud in a unified schedule. Weather is built into its List, Day, Week and Month views, and can be enabled under Settings → Weather Options.

Weather is documented under Calendars Premium; verify the current subscription entitlement in the app. 
Calendars Knowledge Base
+1

Trade-off: Less emphasis on advanced weather features such as minute-by-minute precipitation.

Official weather setup guide

3. Calendar 366

Best for Apple-centric users wanting a purchase option

Supports direct iCloud, Google, Outlook and Microsoft 365 accounts, as well as calendars already configured in iOS. Weather is displayed in calendar views using Apple Weather, with current-location or custom-location options.

Free basic version, a 7-day premium trial, and subscription or one-time purchase options. 
Documentation
+1

Trade-off: Direct iCloud account setup requires an Apple app-specific password; using system calendars is an alternative.

Official integration and weather documentation

4. Apple Calendar

Best free option if weather can be separate

Apple's built-in app can display iCloud, Google and Exchange events together. But it doesn't provide the same built-in forecast overlay as the three apps above.

For weather, use Apple's Weather app separately or subscribe to a third-party weather calendar feed, which adds forecast entries as events rather than a native forecast display.

One important difference: a calendar account integration is not a weather integration. An app may sync three calendar providers perfectly but still lack weather forecasting. Conversely, weather powered by AccuWeather or Apple Weather can be built into a calendar app without you needing to install or configure a separate weather calendar.

Which one should you choose?

Choose Fantastical if weather is central to planning outdoor events, travel or meetings. Its event-location forecasts and advanced precipitation features make it the strongest weather-focused option.

Choose Calendars by Readdle if you mainly want one clean calendar showing work, family, tasks and weather together.

Choose Calendar 366 if you prefer Apple Weather integration and want the option of a one-time purchase rather than an ongoing subscription.

Stay with Apple Calendar if avoiding additional software and subscriptions matters more than having weather directly in the calendar.

My first two to try would be Fantastical and Calendar 366. Both support the three calendar ecosystems, and their weather features are well documented by their developers.

One setup tip: when connecting your accounts directly inside a third-party app, check whether it's also importing the same accounts from iOS. Otherwise, events may appear twice. Fantastical explicitly documents how to avoid this. 
FAQ

You can also connect Google Calendar directly to ChatGPT to review your schedule and plan around commitments in conversation. That is a separate integration, not a replacement for the calendar apps above.
